column1: # Rows db.tchar.* (line RG-KB item 9(b)): databases whose stored definition-line titles hold bytes outside ' ' to '~' (tests/db_search/tchar, make_tchar.py; README.md there, section "Titles with bytes outside the visible ASCII range"), the five programs: in outfmt 8, 9, 11 and 12 NCBI reads a reported subject's definition line only where it makes the Seq-aligns of its query batch (GetSeqIDs, through the volume's cache of 256 header records by OID), and posts Error: (803.7) [<program>] Blast-def-line-set.E.title / Bad char [0x..] in string at byte N / the title for each such byte at each read that the cache does not answer (N the position after the whole title in its record; the bytes before it already '#'); rows .mb.* split the queries into batches (BATCH_SIZE), .big.* hold OIDs 256 apart (one cache slot) read in both orders and with a clean record of the slot between, .bigal.* an alias of two volumes of 300 (a cache per volume, by the volume's OIDs), .alias.* a second volume, .dmg.* a header NCBI cannot read after a post in one batch (the posts before NCBI's error, in any format), .ps.* parsed Seq-ids, .u8.* a UTF8String title in an earlier batch, .x.* titles of 300 and 1,100 bytes and a NUL; rows of item 9b-2 (outfmt 6, 7, 10, 17, and 8 with PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=2147483647): each batch's prefetch loads each subject once, in Seq-id handle order (OID 0 last), unless NCBI's cache of 10 released blobs still holds it from a batch before (a load reads the header through the cache, then registers the ids of the header its Bioseq holds, which posts unless a second volume wrote it again), and each row whose fields read the definition line (sall* ids, taxonomy, stitle, salltitles) posts again; the losat-rejection rows are formats whose prefetch or formatter reads the definition line where LOSAT does not write NCBI's posts, the prefetch off, and parsed Seq-ids with the prefetch (LOSAT's refusal, check_reported_title).
